topic: Atilius's amphitheatre (AD 27): at Fidenae a cheaply built wooden arena packed with crowds starved of gladiator shows under Tiberius gives way, burying spectators and bystanders while families search the ruins day and night

research_sources.institution: Perseus Digital Library, Tufts University (Tacitus, Annals 4.62, Church & Brodribb translation)
focus: failed to lay a solid foundation

research_cautions: Tacitus gives 50,000 killed or maimed; Suetonius gives over 20,000 dead. Both are ancient figures that cannot be verified; say 'tens of thousands, by Roman accounts' rather than a precise toll.
The translation spells the town 'Fidena'; the modern name is Fidenae.
Tacitus blames Atilius's poor foundations and weak joints; the Senate later exiled him and imposed wealth and ground-testing rules (Annals 4.63).
